mechanism_narrative: A sustained multi-week rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects deepening habituation to staying home, which suppresses discretionary retail trips and keeps RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 22.1 to 31.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise or plateau at elevated levels.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rebounds by more than 15 points week-on-week, it signals households resuming outdoor errands and local outings, which spills over into modestly higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -38.4 to -17.7 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a PARKS rebound exceeding the 15-point threshold, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: Joint continued declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate reinforced restrictions on commuting and workplace attendance, which compound to further depress retail footfall over the next four weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES hit new lows at t-0w (-79.4 and -76.0)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 28 days even as both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to decline jointly.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active strict lockdown regime, RETAIL_REC has reached a behavioral floor near -80; absent any policy change, it cannot fall meaningfully further and will remain flat or tick down slightly over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC has been below -78 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged -81.7 to -82.0 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves more than 5 points in either direction within one week absent any reported policy change in the admissible snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: Improving spring weather in April increases outdoor park visits, and this seasonal uplift in PARKS mobility gradually bleeds into nearby retail and recreation trips, nudging RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -38.4 to -17.7 over the last two weeks despite lockdown
failure_condition: PARKS continues rising while RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized around -36 to -38 after its initial stockpiling-driven collapse, indicating households have settled into a routine of infrequent essential trips; this reduced trip frequency generalizes to retail, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change stays within 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved only -37.1 to -35.7 to -37.7 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises materially over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable within the 3-point band.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops below -80 week-on-week, it signals a tightening of movement restrictions that will mechanically suppress retail visits requiring travel, lowering RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -80 in a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -79.4 at t-0w, approaching the -80 threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses below -80 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following week.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising RESIDENTIAL mobility and falling WORKPLACES mobility jointly signals extended compliance with stay-at-home policy, reinforcing each other to depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks more than either trend alone would imply.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 31.1 while WORKPLACES fell to -76.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues rising and WORKPLACES continues falling together.
